headline: Recommended City Council permits for National Grid poles and cables on Washington, Adams Hill, and Highland, and CommLink fiber conduit on Blackburn Drive
summary: All six votes were 3-0, and each recommendation carries Public Works conditions, such as 72 hours' notice before work starts and trench patching. National Grid is replacing primary cables along 1.5 miles of Washington Street, and some poles are being replaced because their supports were anchored to dead trees. Two items were continued: a zoning amendment to December 2, 2026, and a Madison Avenue pole petition to November 18, 2026.

Planning & Development                           November 4, 2026                                 Page 1 of 12
Planning & Development Standing Committee
Wednesday, November 4, 2026 – 6:00 p.m.
City Hall
1st Floor Council Conference Room
9 Dale Avenue
Gloucester, MA 01930
-Minutes-
Planning & Development Committee Present: Chair, Councilor Jason Grow; Vice Chair, Councilor
Dylan Benson; Councilor Hannah Kimberley
Also Present: Legislative Aide, Lynds Jones
This meeting was conducted in person and remotely through ZOOM
Councilor Grow called the P&D meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
Councilor Grow announced the names of the P&D Committee members in attendance.
1. PP#2026-006: Petition by National Grid to install 1 JO pole on Washington Street beginning at 
a point approximately 160 feet Southwest of the centerline of the intersection of Washington 
Street and Woodbury Street. Installing a new stube pole P342-84 40’ South-East of P342. 
Gloucester, MA. 
PP#2026-007: Petition by National Grid to install 1 JO pole on Washington Street beginning at a
point approximately 687 feet Southwest of the centerline of the intersection of Washington Street
and Woodbury Hill. Installing a new stube pole P353-84 46’ East of P353. Gloucester, MA.
PP#2026-008: Petition by National Grid to install 1 JO pole on Washington Street beginning at a
point approximately 596 feet Southwest of the centerline of the intersection of Washington Street
and Woodbury Hill. Installing a new stube pole P354-84 47’ East of P354. Gloucester, MA.
 Public Hearing Opened: 6:05 p.m.
 Speaking in Favor: Councilor Grow stated that these three pole petitions would be taken up as one
public hearing as they were all part of the same project, but separate votes would be taken. Ismail
Mikou, 44 River Street, Beverly stated that this project was part of replacing the primary cables
along 1.5 miles of Washington Street in the City and Granite Street in Rockport. He stated that bare
cables would be replaced with larger covered cables. He stated that because these new cables were
heavier it would require them to replace some poles and install new ones. He stated that some current
poles had mechanical support that was anchored to dead trees, which was not best practice, and the
new poles would fix these issues. 
 Speaking in Opposition: None.
 Communications: Legislative Aide, Lynds Jones read the following memos from the DPW
Director, Michael Hale:
Planning & Development                           November 4, 2026                                 Page 2 of 12
Planning & Development                           November 4, 2026                                 Page 3 of 12
Planning & Development                           November 4, 2026                                 Page 4 of 12
 Questions from Councilors to Applicants/Staff: Councilor Grow asked for clarification on the
instillation of stube poles. Ismail Mikou stated that stube poles would be installed to replace the
mechanical support currently being provided by dead trees.
Councilor Benson asked how long would construction last. Ismail Mikou stated it would take a few
weeks during the middle of 2027. 
 Public Hearing Closed: 6:15 p.m.
Summary of Discussion: None.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Benson,
the Planning & Development Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council

the necessary sustaining and protecting fixtures, along and across the public way, National Grid to install 1
JO pole on Washington Street beginning at a point approximately 160 feet Southwest of the centerline of
the intersection of Washington Street and Woodbury Street. Installing a new stube pole P342-84 40' South-

the following conditions:  
1. Notification to the Department of Public Works 72 hours in advance of the proposed work. A 
construction schedule will be prepared by the applicant for review and acceptance by the 
Department of Public Works.
2. In the absence of a detailed construction plan, the Department of Public Works requests: all 
proposed conduits and appurtenances shall be placed so as to cause minimum conflict with

two lifts of 2-inches, totaling 4- inches.
5. Sidewalks must be restored with like material immediately after pole set.
6. Paving conditions must be approved by Public Works prior to issuance of road opening permit.

2. PP#2026-009: Petition by CommLink Integration Corp. to install underground facilities on
Blackburn Drive approximately 500 feet south of the intersection of Blackburn Drive and Dory
Road, to continue approximately 670 feet west on Dory Road and then south into the 11 Dory
property. 
 Public Hearing Opened: 6:20 p.m.
 Speaking in Favor: Evan Landry, CTO CommLink Integration Corp. stated that the work would
install four-inch conduits for fiber optic cables to connect the Applied Materials buildings. He stated
that there would be handholes every 250 feet. 
 Speaking in Opposition: None.
 Communications: Legislative Aide, Lynds Jones read the following memo from the DPW
Director, Michael Hale:
Planning & Development                           November 4, 2026                                 Page 7 of 12
 Questions from Councilors to Applicants/Staff: Councilor Benson asked how long the project
would take. Evan Landry stated it would take three to four weeks and the work should be done
before the end of 2026.
Councilor Grow asked if the fiber optic cable would be just for use by Applied Materials. Evan
Landry stated it would be an internal connection between Applied Materials’ buildings.
Councilor Grow stated that he would be adding a condition that when final repaving was done, more
than just the trench was paved. 
 Public Hearing Closed: 6:27 p.m.

 Public Hearing Opened: 6:30 p.m.
 Speaking in Favor: Ismail Mikou, 44 River Street, Beverly stated that this work would replace an
older conduit with updated cables that would increase the service from 200 amps to 400 amps.
 Speaking in Opposition: None.

Director, Michael Hale:

weeks and should take one full day to complete work.

 Public Hearing Opened: 6:38 p.m.
 Speaking in Favor: Ismail Mikou, 44 River Street, Beverly stated that the owners of 27 Highland
